description: `apply_update` BUFFERS an op whose dependency has not arrived and retries it as later ops in the same batch land, rather than dropping it while recording its dot. Replica `b` holds only the empty `para` shell; `a` then creates an element `outer` under it, creates a leaf `inner` under `outer`, and edits `inner`. The batch is delivered in strictly REVERSED order (`deliver.order: [2, 1, 0]`) as ONE `apply_update` call, so every op arrives before the op it depends on. A binding with a dependency buffer drains it in a retry loop — the create of `outer` applies, which unblocks the create of `inner`, which unblocks the `LeafEdit` — and `b` renders `deepX`. A binding without one drops what it cannot apply while still recording the dot, so `b` renders `deep` and the following full `sync` returns NOTHING to repair it: both frontiers already hold every op. That is why the fixture carries a second `sync` and still asserts `converged` — the loss is PERMANENT, not eventually repaired, and only the second sync proves the difference. All THREE ops are required and this scenario must not be 'simplified' to two: established empirically, a create-before-its-parent alone does not discriminate in at least one binding, because `apply_op` pushes the child into the parent's child list whether or not the parent exists yet, so the create is accidentally recovered when the parent lands. The `LeafEdit` is the op that is genuinely destroyed, and it needs both creates ahead of it to be out of order. Motivated by lazily-cpp `fb9fc80` (#lzcppapplyupdatelamport), whose `apply_update` never used its dependency buffer.
